240	/-! ## §2. The comparison is an isomorphism when the source is a sheaf -/
241	
242	/-- **The section-free criterion for the sheafification comparison.**
243	
244	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is by construction the sheafification unit
245	`PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C` whiskered with the forgetful functor. A unit of the
246	sheafification adjunction is an isomorphism exactly when its source is already
247	a sheaf (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`), so the étale sheaf property of
248	`PicSharp.relPresheaf C` suffices — and nothing about `C(k)` enters.
249	
250	Contrast `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`
251	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), which reaches the same conclusion from
252	Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 via a section. The two routes are independent; this one is
253	the one available under the owner decision `I-0491`. -/
254	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k]
255	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
256	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
257	    (h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)) :
258	    IsIso (picEtComparison C) :=
259	  haveI : IsIso (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C) := isIso_toSheafify _ h
260	  Functor.isIso_whiskerRight _ _
261	
262	/-- **Representability makes the relative Picard presheaf an étale sheaf.**
263	
264	Two steps, both structural. A functor represented by a scheme is a sheaf for
265	the subcanonical étale topology
266	(`GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable`, using
267	`subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver`); and the sheaf property of the
268	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued `relPresheaf C` is *equivalent* to that of its
269	underlying type-valued functor `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _`, because
270	the forgetful functor of a concrete algebraic category preserves limits and
271	reflects isomorphisms (`Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget`).
272	
273	The hypothesis is a `RepresentableBy` for an arbitrary `X`, not for
274	`PicScheme C`, so this does not silently consume the seam. -/
275	theorem relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy {k : Type u} [Field k]
276	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
277	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
278	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
279	    (rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
280	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) := by
281	  haveI : (picSharp C).IsRepresentable := ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩⟩
282	  have hsh : Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picSharp C) :=
283	    GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable _
284	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget (s := CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}),
285	    CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type]
286	  exact hsh

288	end PicScheme

290	/-! ## §3. The transport, with no rational point anywhere -/
291	
292	/-- **The transport: a scheme representing `picSharp C` also represents
293	`picEt C`, with no hypothesis on `C(k)`.**
294	
295	This is the statement the seam docstring and the board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`
296	declare impossible without a section. The proof composes §1 and §2: the
297	representing scheme makes `relPresheaf C` an étale sheaf
298	(`relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`, i.e. subcanonicity), being a sheaf
299	makes the sheafification unit an isomorphism
300	(`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf`), and `Functor.RepresentableBy.ofIso`
301	carries the representation across it.
302	
303	Note what is and is not proved. `X` is *given* here — the theorem consumes
304	`picSharp` representability rather than producing it, and that antecedent is
305	exactly the undischarged output of the Milne–Kollár campaign. What the theorem
306	establishes is that no *further* representability theorem is needed on top of
307	the campaign, contradicting the "eleventh item" pricing. -/
308	noncomputable def picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport {k : Type u} [Field k]
309	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
310	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
311	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
312	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
313	    (PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X :=
314	  rep.ofIso (@asIso _ _ _ _ (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)
315	    (PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf C
316	      (PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy C rep)))
317	
318	/-- **Clause (1) of the seam follows from its `picSharp` analogue.**
319	
320	Same content as `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport`, packaged in the
321	seam's own existential shape so the comparison with
322	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is direct: the local-finiteness and
323	separatedness conjuncts are carried across unchanged, because the transport
324	does not move the representing scheme — it is the *same* `X`.
325	
326	The hypothesis is stated as the `picSharp`-shaped existential rather than as
327	`[HasPicScheme C]`, deliberately: `HasPicScheme` pins the witness to
328	`PicScheme C` and has no instance, so quantifying over it would make this
329	theorem consume an uninhabited class. Here the witness is universally
330	quantified and the statement is a genuine implication. -/
331	theorem hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
332	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
333	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

335	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
336	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) :
337	    ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
338	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
339	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by

344	than the seam's own second conjunct `HasRationalPoint C → IsIso …`.

Unfolding a typeclass into chart language feels like a reduction and is not. Measured
2026-07-29 (AJC run 0084 r2, my own claim, refuted by a `work-reviewer` audit; I
reproduced the refutation before accepting).

The leaf was `SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f`. `HasRingHomProperty.iff_appLE` turns it
into a condition on affine chart pairs. I stated `.mpr` of that as a reduction with **no
smoothness hypothesis** and concluded "the leaf is one obligation, the smoothness half is
absorbed". Two defects:

- the hypothesis has no smoothness in it because `iff_appLE`'s right-hand side **is** the
  class. Nothing was absorbed. The absorption lemma I cited as the mechanism
  (`IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isStandardSmooth`) was invoked by **no
  declaration in my own file** — `#print` on the theorem showed the body was exactly
  `(iff … ).mpr h`.
- the unfolded form was **harder** than the class. `SmoothOfRelativeDimension`'s field is
  *pointwise-existential* (`∀ x, ∃ U V affine, …`): one chart pair per point. The `iff`'s
  RHS demands the condition at *every* pair. So I pointed the next prover at more work
  than mathlib asks.

**How to apply:** before calling any `iff`-derived statement a reduction, `#print` the
theorem and read its body — if it is `.mpr` of an unfolding, say so in the docstring.
Then `#print` the **class** and compare quantifiers: if the class field is
`∀ x, ∃ …` and your hypothesis is `∀ …`, you have strengthened, not reduced. The honest
target is usually the anonymous constructor over the pointwise form.

Corollary I also got wrong in the same file: a failing `inferInstance` for a
`HasRingHomProperty` is not a mathematical absence — the proposition may be a library
`iff` ([[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]]). And an equality proved by one `rw` that
holds for an *arbitrary* property carries no content about the property you care about;
check genericity before drawing a conclusion from it, or you will dismiss a live route
(I dismissed homogeneity, which the pointwise field makes exactly the right route).
See also [[obligations-list-is-names-not-distances]].
